elements.label: Figure 1.10
elements.description:
Stacked column chart, distribution of economic classes as share of the population (%). Y-axis: "Share of the population", 0 to 100 in steps of 20. X-axis: years 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, 2018, 2020. Legend: Extreme poor (teal), Moderate poor (orange), Economically vulnerable (gray), Economically secure (yellow), Middle-class (blue). No values are printed on the chart; approximate readings by segment (bottom to top: Extreme poor, Moderate poor, Economically vulnerable, Economically secure, Middle-class):
2010: ~4, ~13, ~31, ~43, ~9 (total 100)
2012: ~2.5, ~11, ~27.5, ~50.5, ~8.5
2014: ~2.5, ~8.5, ~24, ~55.5, ~9.5
2016: ~2, ~6.5, ~20.5, ~58, ~13
2018: ~2, ~5, ~16.5, ~59.5, ~17
2020: ~1, ~4, ~14, ~58, ~23
The pattern: extreme poor and moderate poor shares shrink steadily, the economically vulnerable share falls sharply, and the middle-class share rises from about 9% to about 23%.

elements.label: Figure 1.11
elements.description:
Stacked column chart, distribution of economic classes as population in millions. Y-axis: "Population (in millions)", 0 to 100 in steps of 20. X-axis: years 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, 2018, 2020. Legend: Extreme poor (teal), Moderate poor (orange), Economically vulnerable (gray), Economically secure (yellow), Middle-class (blue). No values are printed on the chart; approximate readings by segment (bottom to top: Extreme poor, Moderate poor, Economically vulnerable, Economically secure, Middle-class):
2010: ~3.5, ~11.5, ~25.5, ~38.5, ~7.5 (total ~86.5)
2012: ~2.3, ~9.7, ~25, ~44.5, ~7.5 (total ~89)
2014: ~2.3, ~8.2, ~22, ~50.5, ~9 (total ~92)
2016: ~1.5, ~6.5, ~19, ~53.5, ~13 (total ~93.5)
2018: ~1.5, ~5, ~16.5, ~57, ~17 (total ~97)
2020: ~1, ~3.5, ~14, ~56, ~23 (total ~97.5)
The total population rises over the period, the middle-class count roughly triples from about 7 to about 23 million, and the extreme poor and moderate poor counts decline.
